evidence: The data for our case study spans over thirty years of articles from the New York Times, from January 1986 to December 2015, and was originally collected by BIBREF68 BIBREF68. The articles come from all sections of the newspaper, such as “World", “New York & Region", “Opinion", “Style", and “Sports". Our distributional semantic methods rely on all of the available data in order to obtain the most fine-grained understanding of the relationships between words possible. For the other techniques, we extract paragraphs containing any word from a predetermined list of LGTBQ terms (shown in Table TABREF19).

title: A Framework for the Computational Linguistic Analysis of Dehumanization
answer_short: They identify discussions of LGBTQ people in the New York Times by analyzing linguistic correlates of dehumanization, including negative evaluations, denial of agency, moral disgust, and vermin metaphors, using computational linguistic methods.
answer_rationale: The document describes a computational linguistic framework developed to analyze dehumanizing language in discussions of LGBTQ people in the New York Times. This framework identifies linguistic correlates of key components of dehumanization—such as negative evaluations, denial of agency, moral disgust, and vermin metaphors—and applies these methods to analyze the New York Times articles from 1986 to 2015. The framework uses various computational techniques, including valence analysis, connotation frames, word embeddings, and dominance scores, to quantify these components across different time periods and labels (e.g., gay vs. homosexual).
